modules.module_title: Manage preparatory activities for forging operation

pcs.pc_description: Choose the appropriate material for the forging process based on the desired properties, such as strength, durability, and heat resistance.
Cut or shape the raw material into the initial form called a billet or blank. The size and shape of the billet will depend on the final part's design.
Heat the billet to the appropriate forging temperature. The temperature is critical for ease of deformation and material flow during forging. Use a furnace or other heating equipment.
Design and fabricate the forging dies or tooling required for the specific part. The dies should be designed to shape the material according to the part's design.

Apply lubricants to the die surfaces and billet to reduce friction and facilitate material flow during forging. Lubrication helps prevent excessive wear on the dies and enhances the quality of the forged part.
Set up the forging equipment, such as hammers, presses, or hydraulic machinery, ensuring they are in proper working condition and aligned correctly.
Train the operators who will be performing the forging process. Skilled operators are essential for achieving accurate and consistent results.
Implement safety measures to protect operators from hazards associated with forging, such as hot materials, heavy equipment, and potential flying debris. Provide appropriate safety gear and training.
Ensure the forging workspace is clean and organized. Properly store materials, tools, and safety equipment for efficient and safe operations.
Mark or identify the workpiece or billet with any necessary information, such as part numbers, heat codes, or other traceability markings.
Develop and document quality control plans that outline the specific inspection and testing procedures to ensure the final product meets the required specifications.
Establish the sequence of forging operations, including the number of strikes, rotations, and manipulations required to achieve the desired shape.
Inspect and verify that all preparation activities have been completed according to the forging plan and quality control requirements.
Use appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for safe working in work area
Carry out process safety measures as per industry specifications
Place the heated billet on an anvil or flat surface between the open dies.
Apply compressive forces to the billet using a power hammer, press, or other forging equipment.
Deform the material and shape as it flows between the open dies.
The workpiece may need to be manipula ted and rotated between strikes to achieve the desired shape. Skilled operators use techniques such as bending, twisting, and tapering to shape the material.
Continue forging the workpiece in a series of strikes until the desired shape and dimensions are achieved.
Reheating the billet if it cools down during the process.
Trim any excess material or flash from the forged part, which may have been forced out during the forging process.
Allow the forged part to cool naturally or use controlled cooling processes to relieve residual stresses and prevent cracking.
Inspect the forged part for defects, adherence to specified dimensions, and quality standards.
Perform any necessary surface treatments or finishes, such as shot blasting, machining, or coating.
Conduct quality checks and tests to ensure the part meets the required specifications and standards.
Inform concerned authority in case of any abnormalities observed during execution of work
